priorities.hero_headline: People before power, on every block of Ward 6.
priorities.hero_sub: Three commitments, in plain words. Cassandra has no voting record yet, so instead of boasting she is promising, and she wants you to hold her to it.
priorities.p1_desc: Everyone in Ward 6 has the right to feel safe at home, on the way to work and at the park down the street. Safety is built when neighbors, city staff and public safety agencies work together and answer to the people they serve.
priorities.p1_desc2: Accountability means residents can see what is being done in their name and can speak up when it falls short. It is not about being for or against anyone. It is about results that neighbors can feel.
priorities.p1_desc3: Cassandra will bring residents into the conversation early, not after decisions are made.
priorities.p1_item1: Hold open ward meetings every month, where neighbors can raise safety concerns face to face.
priorities.p1_item2: Push for public safety that is centered on the community, with clear ways for residents to give feedback and see what changes.
priorities.p1_item3: Ask for regular, public reporting on safety in Ward 6 so residents are not left guessing.
priorities.p1_item4: Work with neighbors and block groups on practical fixes, like lighting, safe routes and places to gather.
priorities.p2_title: Dignity and practical solutions for unhoused neighbors and struggling families
priorities.p2_desc: Our unhoused neighbors and struggling families are not problems to move out of sight. They are people who deserve practical solutions and dignity. Many of us are one emergency away from the same place.
priorities.p2_desc2: Cassandra believes a dignified response starts with listening to the people affected, and with working alongside neighbors, service providers and the city instead of around them.
priorities.p2_desc3: Solutions that last connect people to housing, work and help, and treat them with respect along the way.
priorities.p2_item1: Work with neighbors, service providers and the city on a dignified response to homelessness that goes beyond moving people along.
priorities.p2_item2: Make it easier for families in Ward 6 to find the help that already exists, in English and in Spanish.
priorities.p2_item3: Listen to people who have lived through hard times, and make sure they are heard at City Hall.
priorities.p2_item4: Speak up for stronger, better-funded services when the city sets its budget.
priorities.p3_title: Investment in neighborhoods, youth, and the services that help people thrive
priorities.p3_desc: A thriving Ward 6 is one where a kid has somewhere good to go after school, a family can count on the services they need, and a neighborhood is cared for. That takes investment, not just promises.
priorities.p3_desc2: Cassandra will push for city dollars to reach the neighborhoods and programs that make daily life better, and she will ask residents where to start.
priorities.p3_desc3: She will explain her votes and her budget priorities in plain language, so nobody has to guess where the money goes.
priorities.p3_item1: Push for more for kids to do, from after-school activities to summer programs.
priorities.p3_item2: Ask residents to help set priorities for neighborhood investment, then report back on what happens.
priorities.p3_item3: Advocate for the services that help Aurora residents thrive, including libraries, parks and support for families.
priorities.p3_item4: Back small businesses and local hiring that keep opportunity in the neighborhood.
priorities.how_title: A promise about how, not just what
priorities.how_listen_text: Regular ward meetings, held where neighbors are, so your voice is heard before decisions are made.
priorities.how_transparency_text: Every vote made public and explained, so you always know how I voted and why.
priorities.how_access_text: Bilingual office hours in English and Spanish, so every neighbor can reach me.
priorities.how_independence_text: Powered by everyday people, not corporations. I will answer to neighbors, not donors.
priorities.cta_title: Help build a Ward 6 that puts neighbors first.
priorities.cta_text: The primary is February 23, 2027. Volunteer, donate, or tell a neighbor. Every bit of it counts.
